# ADR-0007 — One boxed value representation in generated bytecode

- **Status:** accepted
- **Date:** 2026-11-04
- **Deciders:** oq-compiler, oq-architect
- **Related:** ADR-0003, ADR-0006

## Context

T-0056 had to emit branches and loops. Class file version 50 and above are verified by type
checking, so any method with a jump needs a `StackMapTable` whose frames describe the exact
type of every local and every stack entry at every join point. That is the part of bytecode
generation that produces `VerifyError`s, and the failure surfaces at run time, not at build
time.

Oqthara is dynamically typed. A variable can hold a `Long` and later a `String`, and `1 and 2`
must be `true`. The interpreter implements this by boxing everything as `Object` and routing
all semantics through `Values`. Three representations were considered:

1. **Unboxed primitives when provable.** `Long` variables live in `lload`/`lstore` slots,
   integers in `iload`/`istore`, with frames carrying `long`, `int` and so on.
2. **Specialized methods per static type**, generating several variants of each method.
3. **One boxed representation**, where every value is a reference and every frame is
   `java/lang/Object`.

## Decision

Use one boxed representation.

Every local is an `astore`/`aload` slot, every operand is a reference, and every
`StackMapTable` frame is a `full_frame` naming `java/lang/Object` for each local with an empty
stack. Arithmetic, comparison, equality and truthiness call static helpers on
`dev.oqthara.runtime.Arithmetic`, which delegate to the same `Values` methods the interpreter
uses.

Locals are initialized to `null` in a prologue so that no slot is ever `top` at a join point.

## Consequences

Positive:

- One frame shape is valid at every label, so there is essentially one place to get stack
  maps wrong instead of a combinatorial set of type states.
- Compiled and interpreted arithmetic cannot drift, because both call `Values`. The
  conformance parity test enforces this over 41 programs.
- Type changes at branch joins are free: `x = 1` then `x = "a"` needs no new frames.

Negative:

- Arithmetic boxes `long` results (`Long.valueOf`) and unboxes on every operation, so
  compiled code is not faster than the interpreter for numeric loops yet. This is a known and
  documented limitation, not an oversight.
- `Integer`/`Long` distinction is invisible in frames, so a future unboxing optimization must
  add real type states and frames per parameter.
- Local slots are never reused across sibling scopes. A method with many small blocks uses
  more slots than strictly necessary; this is bounded by the 255-slot check.

## Alternatives rejected

**Unboxed primitives when provable** is the eventual destination for performance, but doing
it before functions, exception handlers and interop compile would mean writing and debugging
the frame generator three times. It belongs in a dedicated optimization task after the
compiled subset covers real programs, with benchmarks to justify the complexity.

**Specialized methods per type** multiplies the number of emitted methods and complicates
calls across modules, for a benefit the interpreter does not need yet.
